message.content:
You are one of six parallel tracks building v5 of the Wisp plugins (repo orin-dx/wisp-plugins). Your track: BUILD THE NEW CORE PLUGIN `wisp`. Others delete the eight old plugins, remove Codex, build `wisp-packs`, tidy, and clean other repos; stay inside your files.

## Setup
`/usr/bin/git fetch -q origin` (network: dangerouslyDisableSandbox true), then work from origin/main (your worktree may start elsewhere; run `/usr/bin/git merge --no-edit origin/main`). Read AGENTS.md, shared/constitution.md, docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md (architecture B and the strategic layer; this is your spec), docs/adr/README.md and ADRs 011 to 017, shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md (how to write the ADR), and the sources you will draw from: plugins/sentinel (exit-gate, verifier, recon), plugins/ranger (adversary, recon, hazard references), plugins/smith (implement, spike, reviewer), plugins/guide (the six commands), plugins/scribe and plugins/navigator (spec and plan rules), shared/hooks/*.py, shared/references/**, docs/evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md.

## Decisions already made (treat as given)
- v5 is four plugins: `wisp` (core, yours), `courier`, `muse`, `mason`, plus `wisp-packs` (another track). Claude Code only (Codex and Antigravity are being removed). The eight old plugins (weaver, vanguard, scribe, navigator, smith, sentinel, ranger, guide) are deleted by another track; you take what is worth keeping from them as new content in `wisp`.
- Principles: agents are not a team of people; prescribe outcome, constraints and evidence bar, not steps; must-hold rules go in deterministic checks; independent verification only where a confident mistake is costly or irreversible; autonomy and review scale with reversibility; humans see artifacts only at the edges (brief and decision cards in; diff or render, evidence, a list of what was not verified, PR or changelog out); no human ceremony (no mandatory spec, plan or sign-off stages).
- Agent structure: constitution block (byte-identical, copy from an existing agent), optional `<load_first>`, `<goal>`, `<judgment>`, `<output>`; EARS only in `<output>`; agent descriptions at most 450 characters and name the skill that starts them; tiers from the constitution (haiku/low, sonnet/medium, opus/high).

## Deliver (you own these files: plugins/wisp/**, shared/references/work/** (new), shared/hooks/stop-check.py (new), shared/hooks/validate-handback.py, tests/test_wisp_*.py, docs/adr/018-*.md and its index row)
1. `plugins/wisp/` with plugin.json (id `wisp`, version 1.0.0; copy the author block and fields from another plugin), README, CHANGELOG, the `shared -> ../../shared` symlink, and hooks/hooks.json.
2. Skills: one `work` skill that classifies the change by reversibility and blast radius (contained, shared, irreversible), states outcome, constraints and evidence bar before work, picks review depth and the modes (explore, spike, fix, build, check, ship), asks the owner only for decisions that change scope or are irreversible (decision cards), and hands off to `muse:sketch`/`muse:promote` for exploration and `courier` for shipping. Plus six one-line alias skills (`explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship`) that start `work` in that mode. Descriptions lead with the situation and at most 450 characters.
3. Agents: `verifier` (opus/high: fresh context; gets the brief, the diff and the evidence list, not the worker's reasoning; checks claims against code, a build or a render by running it; returns `verdict@3` with the existing rules: two rounds, evidence-citing blockers, escalate a repeated blocker, outcome-versus-baseline claims pending without a comparison run), `adversary` (opus/high: tries to refute one finding or claim; adapt ranger's adversary), `recon` (haiku/low: read-only inventory of stack, commands and entry points; adapt the existing recons). Keep these to what is needed; no other agents.
4. Shared references under shared/references/work/ (new files, each at most 120 lines): the modes and tiers, decision cards, the verifier brief, and a short "when a spec or plan is worth writing" note that points to the existing spec and plan conventions. Reuse existing references where they fit instead of copying them.
5. Hooks: (a) `shared/hooks/stop-check.py`: a Stop hook that, when the working tree has uncommitted changes and the final message has no "Not verified" statement, blocks stopping once with a short reason (use stop_hook_active to avoid loops; fail open on any error; stdlib only); register it in plugins/wisp/hooks/hooks.json. (b) Update shared/hooks/validate-handback.py: route `wisp:verifier` to verdict@3 and remove routes for the plugins being deleted; keep its tests (tests/test_handback_validator.py) passing and adapted.
6. ADR 018 (docs/adr/018-*.md, the new short scannable form: Decision, Why, Rejected, Consequences with Revisit when, Evidence) superseding ADR 001's per-mode agent structure rationale where it concerns many role agents, ADR 003 (cognitive-mode separation) and ADR 007 (persona ids for ten plugins): state what the v5 structure is and what replaced them; add its index row and set the superseded records' Status/Relation as decision-records.md says.
7. Tests (tests/test_wisp_core.py): structure and description caps for the new agents and skills, hook behavior (stop-check blocks once and fails open), `wisp:verifier` routed, alias skills exist.
8. Add the plugin to marketplace.json (id, name, version, path, description) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (name, description, source `./plugins/wisp`) so `just check` passes in your worktree (another track removes the old entries; the integrator resolves any merge overlap).

## Rules
Keep wording outcome-based and short; no persona or backstory sections. Do not edit plugins other than wisp, README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md or versions (the integrator bumps ecosystem 5.0.0). Run `just claude-manifests-sync` then `just check`; judge by exit code (`just marketplace-sync` may not apply if Codex files are absent; if it is still in your tree and fails on your plugin, skip it and say so). Commit locally with `/usr/bin/git add -A` then a separate `/usr/bin/git commit` with dangerouslyDisableSandbox true (GPG signing; approved), message ending with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01SGj1qDtVs8manZp9LRpuqm`. Use /usr/bin/git for git; avoid the word git in other command text, heredocs and $(...); write scripts with your file tool under your TMPDIR and run by path. Do not push. Report: branch and commit, file list, how the verifier differs from the old gates, hook behavior, checks run, and anything you could not do.

<system-reminder>
Other agents active in this session, addressable via SendMessage({to: name, message}): main, adr-condense, adr-old, adr-scan, audit-docs, audit-harness, audit-projects, backstory-removal, baseline-check, catch-rate, catch-rate-2, ceremony-navigator, ceremony-readiness, ceremony-versions, design-doc, evidence-docs, gate-hygiene, measurement, planner, repo-decisions, repo-tidy, session-data, skill-routing, v5-delete, v5-nocodex.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>
